newsitem.title: USA: Winston-Salem, N.C., to vote on $75 mln GO bonds.
newsitem.headline: Winston-Salem, N.C., to vote on $75 mln GO bonds.

text.p: City aldermen in North Carolina's Winston-Salem set a June 24 referendum on $75 million of general obligation bonds.
Proceeds would finance street and sidewalk improvements, parks and recreation projects, renovations at the Benton Convention Center and housing and economic development projects.
Debt service would be paid by increasing the property tax rate by three cents in fiscal 1999 and by another cent in fiscal 2001. The current rate is 59 cents per $100 of assessed value.
The aldermen unanimously approved the referendum at a Monday night hearing despite protests from a small group of residents who questioned the timing.

Critics said the special election would cost the city more than $100,000 and urged the aldermen to put the bond proposal on the ballot during the September mayoral election, the October primary runoff or the November general election.
